review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The direct Airy estimator and complete-schedule prior support a sharp minimax-value sandwich and the endpoint-transfer theorem, but the advertised derivation of the stratified decision experiment from the exact eight-type orbit game is not delivered. review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The delivered result is a matched global second-order minimax expansion with an explicit Airy constant, finite-schedule upper and all-design Bayes lower constructions, exact bounded-endpoint transfer, and a necessary-and-sufficient local allocation frontier. The open uniform singular bridge does not load-bear on those global value results, and the framing accurately refrains from claiming fiberwise experiment convergence. The package remains confined to one fixed three-arm contrast and does not present the advertised exact n=3 label-gap computation or numerical finite-sample certificates, limiting its significance for a leading econometrics journal. Publication-level reproducibility also requires a precise source for the invoked Airy regularity facts and fuller verification of the q-dependent prior expansions and diagonal uniform-remainder argument. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. [D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves matched global second-order minimax expansions through a schedule-uniform estimator and an all-design Bayes lower bound, but it does not prove the stronger fiberwise liminf/recovery comparison posed in oeq:uniform-singular-bridge; the framing accurately leaves that comparison open. review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The global minimax expansion is supported by a separate schedule-uniform estimator and all-design Bayes-prior sandwich, so the open uniform-singular-bridge question does not leave the stated sharp constant or allocation frontier unproved. What remains unproved is the stronger claim that the stratified face/corner experiment itself arises through a uniform liminf-and-recovery comparison across transverse eta strata; the note delivers only the tangent program, spectral calculation, and global value bounds. The contribution is confined to one fixed three-arm contrast with a common bounded outcome interval, and the nominally computable finite-orbit certificates are not accompanied by actual calculations, code, or finite-sample evidence showing the practical size of the second-order gain. The related-work prose also repeatedly calls recent arXiv preprints “published” and relies rhetorically on a non-archival repository parent, although the essential orbit reduction is reproved in the note. These scope, evidence, and positioning limitations keep the projected paper below the strongest leading-journal contributions despite clearing the field-tier floor. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.9 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
